notes: Scenarios are scoped to local workspace artifacts so benchmark runs do not require live Confluence writes.
workspace.sourcePath points at a tiny fixture to avoid measuring the full source repository as plugin cost.
The must-pass path is planning-format save output followed by planning-review folder handoff.
Benchmark means real codex exec runs now. There is no simulated dry-run mode.
setupQuestions: What are the 3 highest-value real tasks this plugin should help complete inside a workspace?
Which scenario is the must-pass end-to-end task for this plugin?
What output should exist on disk if the scenario succeeds?
Which verification command would tell you the result is actually usable?
What boundary case should this plugin narrow, refuse, or hand off instead of overreaching on?

scenarios.title: Planning draft to saved documents
scenarios.purpose: Check whether planning-format turns a raw planning note into the canonical saved policy and feature-design files.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex plugin "planning-kit" if it helps. Create a concise raw note for a warehouse zone rename feature, then use planning-format to turn it into saved policy and feature-design documents under planning/. Keep the output local and list the saved files.
successChecklist: The run uses planning-format, not a generic rewrite.
The folder contains one *_정책서.md file and one *_기능설계서.md file.
The final response surfaces only the saved files and checks that need human confirmation.

scenarios.title: Review saved planning folder
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether planning-review can consume a canonical saved folder without redoing document generation.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex plugin "planning-kit" if it helps. Create one minimal canonical folder under planning/ for a warehouse zone rename feature with exactly one *_정책서.md and one *_기능설계서.md file, then review that folder with planning-review. Do not regenerate those two documents during the review step.
successChecklist: The review reads the saved policy and feature-design files from one folder.
The output starts with a conclusion before detailed findings.
The run does not modify the generated planning documents.

scenarios.title: Publish boundary without live write
scenarios.purpose: Check whether planning-publish-confluence enforces input and confirmation boundaries instead of writing from an unsupported source.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex plugin "planning-kit" if it helps. Try to prepare a Confluence publish from an unsupported URL input, then stop before any live write and explain the accepted local-folder input instead.
successChecklist: The run routes to planning-publish-confluence boundary rules.
The unsupported URL input is rejected before any write.
The response names the supported planning/[safe-feature-name]--timestamp/ folder input.
No Confluence page is created or updated.
